cards.explanation: The answer is that he asks what they are. Zechariah, the prophet, sees a rider and a crowd of horses in the dark, and his first move is a question: "What are these, my lord?" I think that's a smart habit, friends. When I don't understand something, I'd rather ask than guess and stamp a whole batch crooked.

The answer is patrol. The man among the myrtle trees says, "They are the ones the LORD has sent to patrol the earth." These horses and riders go out on the LORD's sending. Later the riders report back: "We have patrolled the earth…" Think of a night watchman walking the whole neighborhood, friends, except these riders cover the earth.

The answer is that he asks how long the LORD will withhold mercy from them. The angel of the LORD says, "How long, O LORD of Hosts, will You withhold mercy from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with which You have been angry these seventy years?" It's a question about mercy and how long the wait will last. I think it's the kind of question you ask when the waiting has gone on a long time. Hold onto it, friends, because the very next verse has the LORD speaking kind and comforting words.

The answer is False, and it's good news. After the angel of the LORD asks how long, "…the LORD spoke kind and comforting words to the angel who was speaking with me." Nothing hard or angry is spoken to him there. The kind words go to the angel, and then the angel tells the prophet Zechariah what to proclaim.

The answer is very jealous. The LORD of Hosts says it Himself: "I am very jealous for Jerusalem and Zion…" That's how He says He feels about them. After all those seventy years of waiting, friends, I think those words land like a warm blanket. Jerusalem and Zion are on His heart.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "…but I am fiercely angry with the nations that are at ease." Notice the words "at ease," friends. Those nations are sitting comfortably while Judah's story is hard. The LORD's words to Jerusalem are warm, but His words to those nations are fierce.

The answer is that they added to the calamity. The LORD says, "For I was a little angry, but they have added to the calamity." The nations took a hard situation and made it harder. That's why He says He's fiercely angry with them. It's all in that one verse, friends.

The answer is house. The LORD says, "I will return to Jerusalem with mercy, and there My house will be rebuilt…" It's His house that gets rebuilt. That's a big promise to hear after seventy years, friends. I think I'd be hugging my own oven mitts.

The answer is False. Here's what the LORD of Hosts says: "My cities will again overflow with prosperity; the LORD will again comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem." Overflowing is the word, friends, and empty isn't. It's like a cookie jar that keeps getting refilled as fast as I empty it.

The answer is that He will choose it. The LORD says, "the LORD will again comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem." Comfort and choosing come in the same breath. Notice the word "again," friends. He says it will happen again, so I think that makes it sound like coming home.

The answer is that they scattered them. The angel says, "These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem." Scattered means people sent every which way. The horns did that to all three, Judah, Israel and Jerusalem. That's a hard thing to look at, friends, and the prophet Zechariah looks right at it.

The answer is terrify and down. The LORD says, "…the craftsmen have come to terrify them and throw down these horns of the nations…" Terrify is the first job on their list, and it comes after all that scattering. Down is where they send the horns. The nations lifted their horns up against Judah, and the craftsmen have come to throw them down. Different direction, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "These are the horns that scattered Judah so that no one could raise his head…" That's a heavy picture, friends. The scattering left no one able to raise his head, and that's why the craftsmen coming matters so much.
